decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already captures the connector-placement flexibility established for the integrated board.
Removing the former main-board mechanical layout does not change the ESP32 module, full-pin breakout, pitch, or generic-platform requirement, which already includes the integrated-board context.
The immediately preceding client message retains the specific J_BAT short-edge constraint, so the general connector flexibility does not cancel or modify this requirement.

The single-board architecture may obsolete references to the modular main and sensor boards, but the source does not resolve the existing uncertainty about INA versus AXP2101 monitoring or establish the integrated-board measurement topology.

With only one integrated board, the condition of using main-board USB without the power board may be obsolete, but the source does not establish whether the separate LDO is removed or how standalone USB power should now operate.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records removal of the modular interboard interface and deletes its obsolete connector, pinout, and topology attributes.

The source makes the former interboard-cable basis obsolete, but sensors remain externally connected; it is unclear whether the 10–20 cm cable assumption and pull-up placement should be removed, renamed for sensor cabling, or retained.
The only-board decision moves the panel power-button connector onto the integrated board, and removal of the modular J_PWR_SIG interface requires the button to tap the AXP2101 PWRON signal directly.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes, I think they can, now that there is only one board + sensors/buttons/leds which are all easy to position I think there is no issue wherever you put them

decisions.reason: Board-layout consolidation does not change the confirmed ESP32-S3 GPIO assignments or compatibility constraints.
The source does not change the BOOT button, reset connection, or capacitor requirements; these functions remain valid without relying on the removed mechanical constraints.
The existing same-message MODIFY already replaces the three-board enclosure inventory with one integrated board plus the battery, sensors, buttons, and LEDs.
The mechanical-layout removal does not alter the USB-C programming and enumeration behavior, and the preceding constraints continue to require USB-C on the integrated board.
